INTRO07: I've got a plan. Three clear steps, one shared folder... and a phone I appear to have filed somewhere exceptionally secure.
Please tell me the plan isn't on the phone. I've brought an emergency book, but it doesn't cover this.
I can help make it beep. If it's in your hand again, though, I'm counting that as my quickest solve.
CASEWALL12: I can fit all my theories on that wall. I may have to write small around the really important ones.
And the evidence? Or is that going to have to book an appointment?
We could put in a small shelf. Then the theories would look established, even the ones we made up five minutes ago.
For the theories? Mine needs a cushion. It's been standing around waiting for a fact.
A question mark would be more useful. Then I can tell which ideas still need checking when I come back with the next file.
No cushions on the Case Wall. Detective, bring your notes over here. This family has plenty of imagination; let's leave some room for what we can actually prove.
CASE01: Internal stock. No courier. Good. We can check who was at Delivery without inventing anyone new.
Or we investigate my leading theory: a secret tunnel and a minivan. Very efficient. Very suspicious. I haven't decided who drives.
A tunnel, a minivan, and zero evidence. Impressive start, Alio.
Let's park the minivan for a minute and follow the facts first. Detective, there's room for your notes here.
Good. It was blocking mine. If a tunnel turns up later, we'll apologize to the minivan. Until then, it stays in the margin.
CASE02: The Cup has returned itself with suspiciously good posture. Look at it. You'd think it had never left.
It was signed out, Alio. That's allowed. Being polished afterwards is rather grand, but still not a crime.
Then I withdraw my complaint about the Cup. Its paperwork, however, is doing an excellent impression of a blank page.
Better. We need someone who can help explain the missing handoff, not a confession from a trophy. I'll put the return sheet beside your map.
That may be Alio's fastest promotion from theory to useful question. You take the map, Detective. I'll watch the extremely well-behaved Cup.
CASE03: The trophy shelf is trying very hard to look important. I've appointed its brightest sparkle Inspector Glitter.
Has Inspector Glitter found a difference between the photographs, or has it mainly been admiring its own reflection?
Mostly admiring. A difficult first case. I'll compare the pictures while it recovers from not being in charge.
Should I be worried about my job? I can stand by a shelf looking important. I've practiced.
Only if you start shedding glitter. Pass me Photo B, please. Let's give the whole room a proper look before the shelf gets any more attention.
CASE04: That is a very suspicious black box. It's arrived at the wrong tent without looking remotely sorry.
It's a labeled evidence box. The seal is intact. Let's save the interrogation voice for somebody who can answer.
Exactly. Suspicion with paperwork. You have to admire the preparation.
Please don't interrogate the box before the people. Who was with Pixel? That's someone we can actually ask.
May I stare at the box professionally while we find out? I think it's avoiding eye contact.
You've been doing that for a full minute. If it blinks first, it can wear your helmet.
CASE05: I challenge you to beat my locker. I've given it a very stern talk about not embarrassing me.
Does it know this is a competition? Or have you challenged a door without telling the door?
It has been briefed. Begin when you're ready, Detective. The locker and I have cleared our afternoon.
Then we shall read its clues politely. I'd hate to frighten it into forgetting its own code.
If the locker wins, does it get a badge? We'd need somewhere to clip it.
THREAD34: Four marks. One incomplete route. Does this printer ever send anything straightforward? 'Dear Dilo, here is the answer' would be a refreshing change.
You'd complain there was nothing to solve. Then you'd check the back in case it had hidden the interesting bit.
Could it at least send something with a name? I've got 'the thing', 'the other thing' and 'the thing we mustn't lose'. My notes are becoming very unhelpful.
I'll take these to the archive. Names, dates and something to compare them with. If the printer asks for me, tell it I'm checking its references.
CASE06: I had emotionally prepared for a dragon tooth. There was going to be a drawing. Possibly a very impressive warning sign.
So had I. None of my plans involved stirring soup with a Roman spoon.
Perhaps the dragon was a cook. We haven't checked its qualifications.
That explains the spoon. My history book's missing the chapter about Roman dragon chefs, though.
We have a label and an object that disagree. Let's ask about that before we rewrite history.
A relief. I've only just put history back on its shelves.
Can we keep the dragon in the margin? Pencil only. I know you're going to ask.
Good. Leave me room to object. You take the room record, Detective; we'll keep the imaginary dragon out of your way.
CASE07: Alio, how many cupboards have you checked? Please tell me we're counting cupboards, not dramatic entrances.
Only the dramatic ones. I opened the last one very slowly in case the moon was hiding behind the coats.
The moon costume is larger than most cupboards. If it were behind the coats, the coats would be standing in the corridor.
Excellent. We've eliminated the little cupboards. I knew all that slow opening would produce results.
A triumph of fieldwork. Let's check the room record next. The brooms and I are running out of conversation.
CASE08: My route is beautifully straight. No unnecessary turns, no wasted walking. Very impressive on paper.
Have you shown it to the walls? They seem to have plans of their own.
The building has rejected my first draft. I was going to discuss it with the wall, but it hasn't offered an appointment.
Read the door signs first. You may find the building is easier to work with when you use its doors.
I'll hold the map. Please don't negotiate with any load-bearing walls. I'm not holding up the roof while you explain your route.
CASE09: You're looking at that symbol as if it owes you an explanation. Do you know it?
I remember something. That's not the same as knowing. Give me the record beside it before I start trusting a memory on its own.
I'll find it. We can check them together. You can keep the dramatic pause while I look.
While we're checking memories, I remember being promised cake on an investigation. Very clearly. Excellent detail.
You promised yourself the cake, Alio. I was there for that announcement.
A very reliable source. Terrible at delivery. I'd like to interview whoever was supposed to bake it. Unfortunately, I believe that's also me.
CASE10: Two teams. One rover. One truly upsetting cable tangle. Nobody move; I can make this considerably more complicated.
Which problem are you solving first? The rover, the cable, or your urge to take something apart?
The access record. We need someone who can help explain it. You may note that I said this before touching a screwdriver.
Correct answer. Disturbing speed. I'll untangle the cable while you recover from being sensible.
Careful. It may have a third owner. And please log that sensible moment separately; I may need it in a future family discussion.
CASE11: Your phone has been living beside the oat bar. I think they were getting quite close.
It was undercover. You can't expect a good investigation to happen in the most obvious compartment.
Does the oat bar know? It's been very quiet about its new colleague.
We protect our sources. And occasionally forget which compartment they're in. This is a complicated profession.
I'd like that entered in the bag report. Preferably next to the bit where you tell us to label everything.
CASE12: Please speak clearly for the notebook. Name, reason for being here, and anything you remember about the password.
Try listening before your next question. It says 'cracker'. I don't think it's finished answering that one.
I've got 'cracker'. It keeps repeating it. At least its statement is consistent.
I think it's set a price. You're trying to run a serious interview and it's trying to order lunch.
I'll ask the handler. My first interview with a snack budget. Please don't tell Alio; he'll start charging biscuits for his theories.
CASE13: My fox theory has one weakness. I'm prepared to hear it, as long as everyone remembers how good the rest of it is.
Pockets? Where was your fox planning to keep the camera?
Several weaknesses. I'm making a list. I had rather hoped the pockets would count as an equipment problem.
Add 'fox operating camera equipment'. And 'somebody teaching it'. This is becoming quite a large project for one fox.
Cruel. Fair. I'll draw it a tiny camera strap, then let it retire from the case with some dignity.
Keep the drawing. Hand me the actual photo. The evidence is still stubbornly unfoxy, and I'd like to finish before you design its uniform.
CASE14: One of these statements has broken the clock. I'd like the clock to know I was on its side.
Or somebody mixed up two moments. Before we arrest the clock, can we check that?
Could happen. I once announced I'd packed lunch. I'd packed three books. I'd been very thorough about the wrong thing.
I remember. Your bag was very well fed. You had to share my lunch, and the books didn't contribute a thing.
Three books? Not even one recipe? I'd have expected better preparation from this family.
Not one on cooking. Next time you can check my lunch before we leave. You've become very thorough since the cake investigation.
CASE15: Next trip: readable name tags. Big letters. Nothing that requires a family meeting to identify.
I was going to suggest satellite tracking. A small dot on a screen for each bag. Possibly a theme tune.
My tags work indoors, don't need charging and won't announce our arrival every time we walk into a room.
Ruthless. You've beaten me with a piece of cardboard. May I at least draw a satellite on mine? I'd like to lose with dignity.
CASE16: That hat could shelter the whole team. If it rains on our next investigation, I know where I'm standing.
It also had an excellent detective underneath it. I brought the hat for company, not for a review of its roof space.
We're finding the photograph's date, not the hat's. Admire it all you like; it doesn't tell us when the picture was taken.
Finally, a sensible Academy policy. My wardrobe has suffered quite enough questioning for one afternoon.
Can we still admire it respectfully? I think Alio wants to add an extra room.
Within controlled limits. One more room and I'm charging rent. Now pass me the photograph, please.
CASE17: Railway-investigation helmet: deployed. Ready for tracks, tunnels and announcements that sound unnecessarily urgent.
It's the same helmet. You wore it to the last investigation.
It has changed departments. Please respect its professional development.
Then perhaps its first assignment can be reading the ticket sleeve. I'd hate to discover we've promoted something that can't read.
Does the helmet earn travel points? Its owner will want to exchange them for snacks.
Only if it buys its own ticket. I am not explaining a separate seat for the headgear.
CASE18: Can your watch accept being wrong, or should I break the news to it privately?
It's handling the news with dignity. No dramatic beeping. A very professional response.
Less gracefully. I'm correcting the record. I'd like it noted that I did this before anyone made me.
I'll check the new times with you. Tell the watch it hasn't lost its job. Please give its owner the same message.
CASE19: I was going to say 'digital ghost'. A good theory, I thought. Very modern. No old-fashioned bedsheet.
Going to? What's happened to it?
I'm checking the scanner first. The ghost can wait outside until we know whether the machine made a mistake.
Look at you. Keeping a perfectly good ghost out of the evidence until it's earned its place.
I'll find it a book while it waits. Something with a proper ending. It must be tired of unfinished business.
A paper one. I'm not giving it the Wi-Fi password. Getting it out of the library would be enough trouble.
CASE20: This panel looks like a very worried pear. I think it's realized we've brought notebooks.
Give it a place on the art wall, not the witness list. We have enough people to question without interviewing the paint.
Understood. Pear excluded from questioning. I'll tell it the good news when it stops looking so nervous.
Does the pear have an alibi? We shouldn't rule it out just because it's having a difficult day.
The pear is paint, Dilo. Please don't make me put that in the notebook.
CASE21: Nobody move the pieces yet. I want to see which edges belong together before we make the message say something we like.
I was going to reach for it again. I'll suggest first. Better for the paper, slightly harder on my patience.
Good. Suggest away. Check the joins with me; if I try to force two edges together, you get to stop me.
And keep the handwriting visible when we sleeve it. Edges first, words next. We'll want to read it without taking the whole thing apart again.
That was a very particular look at the writing. Do you know whose it is?
Maybe. The archive will have to back me up. I don't get to turn a memory into a fact just because I'm the oldest person at the table.
Then you've got the archive, we've got the joins, and Detective has the pieces. I like this plan. I can help without hurrying the paper.
CASE22: Three identical black instrument cases. Excellent. The objects have joined witness protection. We may have to give them new names.
Their names are on the labels. Whoever arranged the protection has made one fairly serious mistake.
Weak cover identities. I could run this operation better with a marker pen and ten minutes.
Please don't improve their labels. They've had a long rehearsal. Let's get them onto the right shelves before you start them on new careers.
I'll check the shelves. I'm not explaining three freshly renamed instruments to their teacher.
CASE23: The arcade scoreboard has challenged me personally. I wasn't even playing. It just sat there showing me a score it knew I'd want to beat.
I've got the wristband file. Can you bear to leave your rival unsupervised while we find someone who can help with the record?
For the case. Tell it I haven't surrendered. And if the score changes while I'm away, I want a witness.
CASE24: I've paused my dramatic theory. It's waiting very patiently. Much better manners than people usually give it credit for.
Yes. The muddy evidence requested a word. I'm trying this new thing where I listen before drawing a tunnel.
Then I'll be quiet too. We've got actual prints to compare, and I want to hear what you notice.
Both of you? I should photograph this. The family will never believe it happened without evidence.
Footprints first. My good behavior can wait for the family album. Put it next to Mom finding her phone; I'd like this album to be fair.
CASE25: This parcel has met more helpful people than it can remember. If one more person says 'Leave it with me', we may need a map of its holidays.
Then let's help it in a less creative order. Check the handoff before anybody moves it again.
I'll guard it. Revolutionary idea: one label, one destination. No unauthorized helping while the Detective works.
What about morale biscuits? For the people. I haven't completely misunderstood the parcel.
Allowed. Bring enough for our Detective too. Advice for the parcel can wait until we've checked where it's meant to go.
THREAD120: I knew we kept those maps for a reason. Our table looks as if we've been collecting paper professionally.
We have. Every one is a solved case. I also kept mine because the stack looked impressive. Both things can be true.
They can. Let's lay out the selected maps before you start measuring your achievements with a ruler.
Useful evidence and an excellent stack. Let him have both.
Then let me have some table. My elbow has become a paperweight. If there's anything else we must keep, you'll have to file me alongside it.
CASE26: Empty rooms. We've been looking at everyone except nobody. I suppose nobody wasn't going to put a hand up.
Nobody has been very quiet. Before we give it a medal, I should mention that it's contributed nothing to the conversation.
Already my favorite witness. No interruptions, no dramatic entrances, and no equipment requests.
Your brothers are right here, Luli. Besides, I've heard you explain a footnote over an entire dinner.
Which I enjoyed. But let's give nobody a turn. Detective, pull the maps closer; I want to see what we've been walking past.
CASE27: Clean hands. Flat map. No heroic folding. This plan is older than all your favorite excuses.
Am I allowed one heroic finger? I only want to point. I can do it at a perfectly sensible distance.
One clean finger, above a landmark. No prodding. The building has survived this long without you poking a new room into it.
We solved a whole parcel mystery, recovered your archive tools and earned permission for one finger. I was hoping for at least a whole hand.
A worthy investment. The sleeve can touch the map; your finger can hover. Now, who's going to help me line up the plans?
CASE28: I've put my tunnel proposal on a separate card. It looks much more convincing with a heading and a straight border.
How much evidence is on the card? I'm asking before you draw a crest for it.
At present? Decorative confidence. I gave that quite a lot of space.
I'd like a card. Some of my very organized plans are mostly that. I've been calling it 'being prepared' and hoping nobody asks for details.
Make it two. I used to call mine 'experience'. That's why I like your question, Luli. It used to annoy me terribly.
CASE29: That's a lot of map. I'll clear some space. Nobody balance anything on the Detective's elbow; I've tried that system and can't recommend it.
Take your time. We're not going anywhere. If you need to stare at one corner for a while, I'll check the other one with you.
I can be quiet for one map. A big one. I'm making a serious offer here.
I've written that down. In pencil, to be fair.
Make the call when you're ready. We're here.
CASE30: No new clue. Use what you earned. Your Case Wall has the record; the panel's ready when you are.
Victory noise? I've been saving a very good one. I'm worried it's going to escape without permission.
Keep it in your head until the door opens. If you're going to celebrate early, at least do it where the rest of us can't hear it.
Mine's already getting loud in there. We can compare them afterwards. Detective gets to hear the door first.
Go on, Detective. You've been with us from the black envelope to this panel. We're right behind you.
